dedupe_keys.name: scenario based seismic risk assessment for central southern malawi bilila mtakataka fault

description: This case study presents scenario-based seismic hazard and risk assessments for Central-Southern Malawi, focused on the area near the Bilila-Mtakataka Fault south of Lake Malawi. It is a paper by Katsu Goda, Panos Kloukinas, Raffaele De Risi, Michael Hodge, Innocent Kafodya, Ignasio Ngoma, Juliet Biggs and Adam Crewe in the proceedings of the 16th European Conference on Earthquake Engineering (Thessaloniki, June 2018; Springer, 22 June 2018), listed in the University of Bristol research portal. The fault is about 130 kilometres long with six segments that might rupture alone or together, so the source models cover several rupture geometries and magnitudes. Building surveys characterise the current stock, and fragility models for typical Malawian masonry buildings are derived from pushover analysis of finite-element models. The combined components give a more accurate baseline of seismic risk. Coverage: Central-Southern Malawi. Access: author manuscript from the Bristol portal; the proceedings volume is from Springer. Licence: publisher copyright; the manuscript is free to read. Caveats: a conference paper; survey data are summarised, not released. Simulation uses: exposure and fragility inputs for earthquake risk in low-income countries. Related records: the Kigali building typology and the Colombian fragility functions.
